newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt market takes positive tone at start.
newsitem.headline: German debt market takes positive tone at start.

text.p: German bonds and Bund futures edged higher in early trading, buoyed by the firmer dollar, and traders said the strong dollar was likely to continue to give the market a positive undertone.

But the focus, temporarily at least, was on German news. The market was waiting for the Ifo economic institute to release its latest forecast, due at 0830 GMT, and for the Bundesbank to set its regular securities tender.
The central bank has already announced that it will set a repo at three percent this week but it could theoretically set a second pact under different conditions.

An announcement by the central bank that it was setting a single tender at an unchanged three percent rate nonetheless had little impact on the market, the focus now moving to next week when the central bank could again signal a policy move.

It could also indicate that it is keeping a tight rein on the market by keeping the market short of liquidity. A move of this type could become evident in this week's repo allocation, which is due on Wednesday.
Dealer said the bund market would also pay close attention to German industrial orders data, expected the next few days.
The September Bund future was trading up 0.11 at 102.27 at 0836 GMT. The benchmark six percent July 2007 bund was at 102.65 bid for a yield of 5.63 percent.
